The search turned up a release note saying automatic resource provisioning is now generally available, though I didn't find a standalone GA announcement.

- **Timeline:** Cloudflare first launched it as an open beta in October 2025, covering KV, R2, and D1 bindings, with wrangler 4.45.0 as the starting version (Automatic provisioning is launching as an open beta; It currently works for KV, R2, and D1 bindings.).
- **GA and expansion:** Wrangler 4.113.0, released July 21, 2026, extended provisioning to Queue, Dispatch Namespace, and Flagship bindings (Deployments can now omit the resource name or ID for these bindings.). The same release dropped the "Experimental:" label from the provisioning header, which signals GA status (Drop the "Experimental:" prefix from the resource provisioning header now that automatic provisioning is generally available.).
- **Behavior:** For Flagship, a binding without an app_id lets Wrangler either connect an existing app or create a new one during deployment, then write the app_id back to the config (Add a flagship binding without an app_id, and Wrangler can connect an existing Flagship app or create a new one during deployment. Wrangler writes the resulting app_id back to your configuration file.).
- **Caveats:** Some docs still show the older "Experimental" flag wording (`--experimental-provision` / `--x-provision`) in a preview style guide, so that page may be stale. The 4.113.0 details come from third-party release aggregators, so the official GitHub release notes or Cloudflare changelog should be checked for the authoritative wording.

content.text:
No, it looks like it's out of beta. Cloudflare launched automatic resource provisioning as an open beta in October 2025, starting with Wrangler 4.45.0, for KV, R2 and D1 bindings. Wrangler 4.113.0 (July 21, 2026) removed the "Experimental:" label from the provisioning output, saying the feature is now generally available. That release also added provisioning for Queue, Dispatch Namespace and Flagship bindings.

I only saw the 4.113.0 details on third-party release trackers, not in an official Cloudflare GA announcement. Check the workers-sdk GitHub release notes to confirm. Some Cloudflare doc pages still show the old experimental flag wording (`--x-provision`), which is probably out of date.

Sources:
- [Cloudflare changelog: Automatic resource provisioning (2025-10-24)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/2025-10-24-automatic-resource-provisioning/)
- [wrangler@4.113.0 release (newreleases.io)](https://newreleases.io/project/github/cloudflare/workers-sdk/release/wrangler@4.113.0)
- [releases.sh: auto-provisioning GA](https://releases.sh/release/rel_6Tt7jAcA0-G8JWWj670Yk-email-routing-addresses-reconciled-on-deploy-auto-provisioning-ga)
